flows.representativeInput: A copy of fixtures/entry-check/clean (an AGENTS.md whose two map paths exist, two context pages) in a temp folder that is not a Git repository, and the same fixture in place inside the prototype checkout; node payload/.joycraft/runtime/entry-check.mjs --root <fixture>, with and without --ci.
flows.expected: Exit code 0; stdout and stderr empty.

observations.actual: The shipped payload command, run directly on the temp copy of the clean fixture, exited 0. The receipt holds both stdout and stderr and has 0 bytes.

Three cases, each exit 0 with stdout 0 chars and stderr 0 chars: the temp copy, the temp copy with --ci, and the fixture in place inside a Git repository. The recorded argv is an inline driver (node -e) that starts each case with no shell, prints its exit code, stdout and stderr to the receipt, and exits 0 only when each exit code is the expected one and each named pair of outputs is equal. The exit codes of entry-check.mjs itself are in the receipt.

findings.summary: A --root that does not exist, or a project with no AGENTS.md and no CLAUDE.md, is "clean": exit 0 and no output, also with --ci (entry-check.mjs lines 78-88; cleanup.mjs line 215 reads only entry files that exist). A CI job with a wrong --root passes without a word. The same receipt shows the two error exits the spec states outside its checks: an unknown argument and an unreadable joycraft.yaml both exit 1 with one stderr line.
findings.assumption: The spec does not decide this case. Reading taken: a project without an entry file has nothing to check, which fits the owner's direction to add no machinery for a rare case.

findings.summary: The check says "the same findings"; the tagged test compares exit codes, the gate findings of the linked tree and the --ci stdout, not the whole JSON (advisory findings) of the two trees. The direct run shows the whole JSON is equal, so the criterion holds; the test could assert run(tree).stdout === run(root).stdout.

trace.mjs for spec 1 in this repository reports all five criteria untraced (entry-clean-silent, entry-dead-path, entry-ci-mode, entry-policy-independent, entry-linked-worktree) with the note "No check inputs are declared": the queue binds no test file, because the tests are in joycraft-prototype and are not vendored. Each of the five has one test with its [AC:<id>] tag in tests/cleanup/entry-check.test.mjs at the pinned commit, and each passed.

The section "Implementation and verification scope" of spec 1 says the gate checks are missing-path and broken-link, every other check is advisory, and the report keeps findings whose path is AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md. The shipped file has five gate checks (line 16 adds script-name, codex-bytes, import), keeps findings by base name, so also a nested AGENTS.md and AGENTS.override.md (lines 14 and 24), and has two more commands, block and lost (line 67). Specs 2, 7 and 10 of the same queue ask for these. No acceptance check of spec 1 is affected.
findings.assumption: The later specs of the queue govern these lines; spec 1 is judged on its five acceptance checks.
